title: Gucci Guilty vs Bleu de Chanel: Which Should You Wear?
summary: Gucci Guilty Pour Femme vs Bleu de Chanel: a warm amber floral against a citrus incense woody. Compare notes, longevity, and best occasions on Scentbird.
body_markdown:
Bleu de Chanel and Gucci Guilty Pour Femme rarely get cross-shopped for smelling alike. They get cross-shopped because both have a reputation as a safe, established pick within their category, and shoppers want to know if “established” means the same thing on both sides. It doesn’t.[Gucci Guilty Pour Femme](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/gucci-guilty-pour-femme-1429) and Bleu de Chanel share almost no notes in common, even though both happen to follow the same basic shape: bright open, warmer close.


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme, available on Scentbird.


## Gucci Guilty Pour Femme vs Bleu de Chanel: what they share


Both fragrances follow the same basic arc even though the ingredients are unrelated: a short, brighter opening gives way within an hour or so to a heavier, warmer base that carries most of the wear time. Gucci Guilty Pour Femme opens on pink pepper before settling into amber and patchouli; Bleu de Chanel opens on citrus and mint before settling into incense and cedar. Both also use that opening mostly as a hook rather than as the point of the fragrance, so judging either one from a strip in the first ten minutes gives a misleading picture of what the bottle is actually for. Both are also considered dependable, widely recognized options in their categories, which is usually why the two end up compared in the first place.


## Gucci Guilty Pour Femme


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme doesn’t sit still long enough to be summed up by its opening alone. Pink pepper and black currant burn off within the first twenty minutes or so, geranium and jasmine take over the middle hours, and by the time patchouli and vanilla settle into the base, the fragrance has effectively changed character three times. Aurelien Guichard composed it for Gucci in 2010, and total wear typically runs seven to nine hours, with the strongest sillage in that first stretch after application. Because the shifts happen fast, smelling it once off a testing strip gives an incomplete picture, and the amber-patchouli finish, is a different fragrance than the fruity one most people notice first. Skip it if you’d rather a scent settle into one identity early and stay there.


## Bleu de Chanel


Jacques Polge composed Bleu de Chanel for the house in 2010 on a base of grapefruit, lemon, mint, and pink pepper, a bright, almost cold opening that dissolves within thirty to forty-five minutes into ginger, nutmeg, and jasmine, before the fragrance settles into incense, cedar, vetiver, sandalwood, and labdanum. The change is dramatic: what starts crisp and citrus-forward ends up smoky and woody, with strong sillage that holds for eight hours or more. The catch is that the citrus brightness people are drawn to at first is the shortest-lived part of the composition, often gone within the first hour, so anyone expecting a fresh scent to last all day gets an incense-heavy one instead. Skip it if a smoky, resinous drydown reads as too heavy for your taste.

## Which is better, Gucci Guilty Pour Femme or Bleu de Chanel?


The differentiator isn’t the shared bright-to-warm arc, it’s what waits at the end of it. Bleu de Chanel’s base is smoky and woody with no real sweetness, built to read as clean and versatile almost anywhere. Gucci Guilty Pour Femme’s base is sweeter and more overtly amber, built for evenings rather than for blending into an office hallway. Anyone deciding between them is really deciding whether they want the ending to smell like incense or like warm amber, since that single choice predicts almost everything else about how each one will be received in a room.


The short answer


Choose Bleu de Chanel if you want a citrus-to-woody fragrance versatile enough for daily rotation. Choose Gucci Guilty Pour Femme if you want a warmer, sweeter amber floral built specifically for evenings and cooler weather.


The shift each one goes through happens over hours, not minutes, so judging either from a single spray will only show half the story.


Give it enough days to show its full character before deciding.

## Frequently asked questions


What does Gucci Guilty Pour Femme smell like?


It moves through three stages: pink pepper and black currant at the start, geranium and jasmine through the middle hours, then amber, patchouli, and vanilla settling in at the base. The character shifts noticeably as it wears.


What does Bleu de Chanel smell like?


Bleu de Chanel opens bright with grapefruit, lemon, mint, and pink pepper, then warms through ginger and jasmine before landing on incense, cedar, vetiver, and sandalwood. It moves from crisp citrus to smoky woods within a couple of hours.


What is the main difference between Gucci Guilty Pour Femme and Bleu de Chanel?


Both open bright and end on a warmer base, but the base itself is different in kind. Gucci Guilty Pour Femme lands on sweet amber and vanilla, while Bleu de Chanel lands on smoky incense and cedar with almost no sweetness at all.


Which lasts longer, Gucci Guilty Pour Femme or Bleu de Chanel?


Bleu de Chanel generally lasts longer and projects more, often past eight hours with a noticeable trail. Gucci Guilty Pour Femme sits closer to seven to nine hours and pulls in closer to the skin sooner.


Is Bleu de Chanel or Gucci Guilty Pour Femme better for the office?


Bleu de Chanel is the safer office choice once its citrus opening settles, since the woody incense base is common and unobtrusive. Gucci Guilty Pour Femme’s amber and patchouli can read as more noticeable in a small, shared space.


Does Bleu de Chanel smell the same all day?


No. The citrus and mint opening is the shortest-lived part of the fragrance, often fading within the first hour, after which it turns noticeably smokier and woodier for the rest of the wear.
